title: CUET Geography Test 4
subject: Geography / Geology (Code: 313)
syllabus_source: CUET SYLLABUS/Geography - 313.pdf (NTA syllabus for CUET (UG) 2026, latest published)
past_paper_reference: Pattern benchmark only: NTA CUET (UG) domain-paper format and public Geography shift analyses (no questions copied)
textbooks: NCERT Class 12 Fundamentals of Human Geography (rationalised)
NCERT Class 12 India: People and Economy (rationalised)
instructions: Each correct answer earns 5 marks; each incorrect answer deducts 1 mark; unattempted questions earn 0.
One set of 5 questions is based on a passage or table; the set stays together.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question: According to NCERT, the three components of population change are:
options: B) literacy, sex ratio and age structure
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) births, deaths and migration
Why: NCERT names births, deaths and migration as the three components of population change; a population grows or shrinks through their combined effect.
Why not the others: (A) are measures of how population is spread; (B) are features of population composition; (C) mixes one component with factors that affect distribution.
Key point: The crude birth rate and crude death rate are both expressed per thousand people.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question: Which of the following is a non-conventional source of energy?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Geothermal energy
Why: NCERT classes solar, wind, hydro-geothermal and biomass energy as non-conventional sources; they are renewable and more evenly distributed.
Why not the others: Coal (B), petroleum (C) and natural gas (D) are conventional, exhaustible fossil fuels.
Key point: Non-conventional sources are also more environment friendly.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Geography: Nature and Scope
questions.sub_topic: Schools of thought in human geography
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (School / approach)
(A) Welfare or humanistic school
(B) Radical school
(C) Behavioural school
(D) Post-modernism

List-II (Main concern)
(I) Questioned grand generalisations and stressed understanding each local context
(II) Lived experience and perception of space by social groups based on ethnicity, race and religion
(III) Used Marxian theory to explain poverty, deprivation and social inequality
(IV) Social well-being of people — housing, health and education
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: the welfare or humanistic school dealt with social well-being (IV); the radical school used Marxian theory to explain poverty and inequality (III); the behavioural school stressed lived experience and the perception of space (II); post-modernism, in the 1990s, rejected grand theories in favour of local contexts (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the welfare and radical schools; (B) swaps the radical and behavioural schools; (D) swaps behavioural and post-modernism.
Key point: The first three schools emerged in the 1970s, in reaction to the quantitative revolution.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question: India's iron ore resources are mainly of two types, both of good quality for industry. They are:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Haematite and magnetite
Why: NCERT notes that the main types of iron ore found in India are haematite and magnetite.
Why not the others: Bauxite and laterite (A) are linked with aluminium; limonite and siderite (B) are lower-grade iron ores not named by NCERT; pyrite and galena (C) are ores of sulphur and lead.
Key point: Most of India's iron ore reserves are in Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka and Goa.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question:
Arrange the following states in descending order of population according to Census 2011:
(A) Bihar
(B) Maharashtra
(C) West Bengal
(D) Uttar Pradesh
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (D), (B), (A), (C)
Why: Census 2011 populations: Uttar Pradesh about 20 crore (D), Maharashtra about 11.2 crore (B), Bihar about 10.4 crore (A), West Bengal about 9.1 crore (C).
Why not the others: (B) puts Bihar above Maharashtra; (C) puts Maharashtra above Uttar Pradesh; (D) puts West Bengal above Bihar.
Key point: Bihar is the densest state but third in total population.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question: India's population in 2011 was about 121 crore, of which about 37.7 crore lived in urban areas. Roughly what share of the population was urban?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 31 per cent
Given: total population ≈ 121 crore; urban population ≈ 37.7 crore.
Step 1: Urban share = 37.7 ÷ 121 × 100.
Step 2: ≈ 31 per cent (NCERT gives 31.16 per cent).
Common mistake: giving the rural share (about 69 per cent, option A), or misplacing the decimal (3.1 per cent, option B).

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: International Trade
questions.question: The act of opening up economies for trading by bringing down barriers such as tariffs, so that goods and services from other countries can compete with domestic ones, is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Trade liberalisation
Why: NCERT defines free trade, or trade liberalisation, as opening up economies by bringing down trade barriers such as tariffs.
Why not the others: Dumping (A) is selling at prices unrelated to cost; protection (B), shielding home industry with barriers, is the opposite of free trade; the balance of trade (D) is the difference between exports and imports.
Key point: Free trade also lets cheaper goods from developed countries compete with local goods, so it needs care.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Tertiary and Quaternary Activities
questions.question: A plumber, an electrician and a technician do not produce goods; they sell their skills. Their work belongs to:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Tertiary activities
Why: NCERT explains that tertiary activities involve the exchange of skills and services for payment; it gives plumbers, electricians, technicians and launderers as examples.
Why not the others: Primary (A) and secondary (B) activities produce or process goods; quinary activities (D) are high-level decision making.
Key point: Tertiary activities depend more on specialised skills and experience than on physical resources.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Planning and Sustainable Development
questions.question: NCERT describes two approaches to planning. In which approach are schemes made for sectors of the economy such as agriculture, irrigation, manufacturing, power and transport?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Sectoral planning
Why: NCERT defines sectoral planning as the formulation and implementation of schemes for developing sectors of the economy; regional planning deals with the development of particular areas.
Why not the others: Regional planning (A) is area-based; target group planning (B) aims at particular groups of people; hill area planning (C) is one target-area programme.
Key point: Regional planning is needed because development has not been even across India.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question: A town with a population of 3,00,000 recorded 4,500 deaths in a year. What is its crude death rate?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 15 per thousand
Given: deaths = 4,500; mid-year population = 3,00,000.
Step 1: CDR = deaths ÷ population × 1,000.
Step 2: 4,500 ÷ 3,00,000 × 1,000 = 15 per thousand.
Common mistake: expressing the answer per hundred (1.5, option B), or dividing population by deaths (66.7, option D).

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Religious group)
(A) Sikhs
(B) Jains
(C) Christians
(D) Buddhists

List-II (Main areas of concentration in NCERT)
(I) Maharashtra
(II) The western coast around Goa and Kerala, and the hill states of Meghalaya, Mizoram and Nagaland
(III) Urban areas of Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra
(IV) Punjab, Haryana and Delhi
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: Sikhs are concentrated in Punjab, Haryana and Delhi (IV); Jains in the urban areas of Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra (III); Christians on the western coast and in the north-eastern hill states (II); Buddhists in Maharashtra (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Sikhs and Jains; (B) swaps Jains and Christians; (C) swaps Christians and Buddhists.
Key point: Hindus form the majority in most states except a few.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Development
questions.question: The basic needs approach, initially proposed by the International Labour Organization, identified six basic needs. Which of the following was NOT one of them?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Employment
Why: NCERT lists health, education, food, water supply, sanitation and housing as the six basic needs; the question of human choices is ignored in this approach.
Why not the others: Health (A), housing (C) and sanitation (D) are among the six.
Key point: Choice and freedom are central to the capability approach, not to the basic needs approach.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Development
questions.sub_topic: Equity as a pillar of human development
questions.question: In India, a large number of women and persons from socially and economically backward groups drop out of school, so their choices are limited. This shows a lack of which pillar of human development?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Equity
Why: NCERT uses this very example for equity — equal access to opportunities for everybody, irrespective of gender, caste or income.
Why not the others: Sustainability (A) is about opportunities across generations; productivity (B) is about human labour productivity; empowerment (C) is about the power to make choices — related, but NCERT gives this example under equity.
Key point: Unequal access to education limits the choices of entire groups.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question: Most of India's coal is of Gondwana age. Where does tertiary coal mainly occur?
options: A) The Damodar valley of Jharkhand and West Bengal
B) The Godavari valley of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh
C) Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya and Nagaland
D) The Mahanadi valley of Odisha
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya and Nagaland
Why: NCERT notes that tertiary coals occur in Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya and Nagaland.
Why not the others: The Damodar (A), Godavari (B) and Mahanadi (D) valleys have Gondwana coal.
Key point: Gondwana coal is about 200 million years old; tertiary coal is about 55 million years old.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport and Communication
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Water transport is much cheaper than land transport for heavy and bulky goods.
Reason (R): Water routes need no construction of the route itself, and the friction of water is far less than that of land, so energy costs are lower.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both are true. NCERT explains that water transport does not require route construction and is cheaper because the friction of water is far less than that of land, which keeps energy costs low — this explains the Assertion.
Why not the others: (B) would need the Reason to be unrelated; (C) and (D) need one statement to be false.
Key point: The oceans are linked with each other and are negotiable by ships of various sizes.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Tertiary and Quaternary Activities
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about tertiary activities:
(A) They involve the commercial output of services rather than the production of tangible goods.
(B) Retail trading includes consumer cooperatives, department stores and chain stores.
(C) Wholesale trading sells mainly to final consumers, in small quantities.
(D) Telecommunication is the slowest means of sending information over long distances.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A) and (B) only
Why: (A) and (B) follow NCERT — tertiary activities produce services, and retail trading reaches consumers through these forms of stores.
Why not the others: (C) is false — wholesale trading is bulk business through intermediaries and supply houses, not through retail stores. (D) is false — telecommunication allows the most rapid flow of information. Every other option includes (C) or (D).
Key point: Trade, transport, communication and services are the four parts of the tertiary sector.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: International Trade
questions.sub_topic: Ports of India and their sites
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Port)
(A) Kochi
(B) Paradip
(C) Kolkata
(D) Tuticorin

List-II (Site)
(I) A riverine port on the Hugli, about 128 km inland from the Bay of Bengal
(II) In the far south of the east coast, in Tamil Nadu
(III) In the Mahanadi delta in Odisha
(IV) At the head of the Vembanad Kayal, a natural harbour
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Kochi lies at the head of the Vembanad Kayal (IV); Paradip is in the Mahanadi delta (III); Kolkata is a riverine port on the Hugli (I); Tuticorin (V.O. Chidambaranar) is in Tamil Nadu (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Kochi and Paradip; (B) swaps Paradip and Kolkata; (C) swaps Kolkata and Tuticorin.
Key point: Kolkata needs constant dredging of the Hugli; Haldia was developed to reduce the pressure on it.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Secondary Activities
questions.question: Industries that process raw materials from fields and farms into finished products for rural and urban markets — such as sugar, pickles, fruit juices and spices — are called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Agro-processing industries
Why: NCERT defines agro-processing as processing raw materials from the field and farms into finished products; its major examples are food processing, sugar, pickles, fruit juices, beverages and spices.
Why not the others: Footloose industries (A) are not tied to raw materials; basic industries (C) supply other industries; high-tech industries (D) depend on advanced research and development.
Key point: Agro-based industries are a class by raw material.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question: Jowar is an important coarse grain of the semi-arid areas of central and southern India. Which state alone produces more than half of India's jowar, according to NCERT?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Maharashtra
Why: NCERT notes that Maharashtra alone produces more than half of India's jowar.
Why not the others: Karnataka (A), Madhya Pradesh (B) and Telangana are other producers, and Rajasthan (C) grows more bajra; none produces as much jowar as Maharashtra.
Key point: Jowar is a rain-fed crop, grown in the kharif season in the north and also in rabi in the south.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Planning and Sustainable Development
questions.question: The Brundtland Report (1987) defined sustainable development as development that:
options: A) achieves the fastest possible growth in national income every year
B) uses natural resources fully until every reserve is exhausted
C) meets present needs without harming future generations' needs
D) depends only on non-conventional sources of energy for growth
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) meets present needs without harming future generations' needs
Why: The World Commission on Environment and Development (Brundtland Report, "Our Common Future") defined sustainable development as development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
Why not the others: (A) ignores the environment; (B) is the opposite of sustainability; (D) is one possible means, not the definition.
Key point: NCERT applies this idea to the Indira Gandhi Canal command area.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the distribution of India's population (Census 2011):
(A) Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state.
(B) About ten states, led by Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Bihar, hold about three-fourths of India's population.
(C) Kerala has a lower density of population than Arunachal Pradesh.
(D) The density of population of India has increased steadily since 1951.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: (A) and (B) follow NCERT, which notes that about ten states hold about 76 per cent of the population. (D) India's density has risen from 117 in 1951 to 382 in 2011.
Why not the others: (C) is false — Kerala is one of the densest states, while Arunachal Pradesh is the least dense (about 17 per sq km). Options (A), (C) and (D) include (C).
Key point: Terrain, climate and water explain much of the variation in density.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question: The HBJ gas pipeline links:
options: A) Hazira in Gujarat with Jagdishpur in Uttar Pradesh, via Bijaipur in Madhya Pradesh
B) Haldia in West Bengal with Jalandhar in Punjab, via Barauni in Bihar
C) Hyderabad in Telangana with Jaipur in Rajasthan, via Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh
D) Hazira in Gujarat with Jamnagar in Gujarat, via Bharuch
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Hazira in Gujarat with Jagdishpur in Uttar Pradesh, via Bijaipur in Madhya Pradesh
Why: NCERT notes that GAIL laid the Hazira–Bijaipur–Jagdishpur pipeline, linking Mumbai High and Bassein gas fields with fertiliser, power and industrial units in western and northern India.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are not the route of the HBJ pipeline.
Key point: Pipelines are the most convenient means of carrying oil and gas over long distances.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question: Indian Railways has been converting metre and narrow gauge lines into broad gauge so that the whole network uses one gauge. This programme is known as:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Project Unigauge
Why: NCERT notes that conversion of metre and narrow gauges into broad gauge is in progress under the Unigauge project.
Why not the others: The Golden Quadrilateral (A) and Bharatmala (B) are road projects; freight corridors (D) are new rail lines for goods.
Key point: Steam engines have been replaced by diesel and electric engines, raising speed and haulage capacity.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question: Which of the following is a means of mass communication rather than personal communication?
options: A) A letter sent by post
D) A text message to a friend
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Radio broadcasting
Why: NCERT divides communication into personal communication (letters, telephone, mobile messages) and mass communication (radio, television, newspapers and films), which reaches millions of people at once.
Why not the others: Letters (A), telephone calls (C) and personal messages (D) are personal communication.
Key point: The internet is used for both personal and mass communication.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: International Trade
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the bases of international trade listed by NCERT?
options: B) Identical resources in every country
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Identical resources in every country
Why: NCERT lists differences in national resources (geology, mineral resources, climate), population factors, stage of economic development, extent of foreign investment and transport as bases of international trade.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are all bases listed by NCERT. If every country had identical climates and resources, there would be little reason to trade.
Key point: Trade arises because countries differ in what they can produce.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Human Settlements
questions.question:
In the Census, towns are grouped into classes by population. Arrange the following classes from the smallest population to the largest:
(A) Class I — 1,00,000 and above
(B) Class III — 20,000 to 49,999
(C) Class IV — 10,000 to 19,999
(D) Class II — 50,000 to 99,999
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (C), (B), (D), (A)
Why: Class IV (C) is smaller than Class III (B), which is smaller than Class II (D), which is smaller than Class I (A).
Why not the others: (A) puts Class II before Class III; (B) starts with Class III; (D) gives the order from largest to smallest.
Key point: A city with a population of one lakh or more is a Class I town; one with ten lakh or more is a million city.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question: Which region does NCERT give as an example of an area inhabited from early periods in history because of its pleasant climate?
options: A) The hot deserts of the Sahara
C) The Arctic and sub-Arctic regions
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) The Mediterranean region
Why: NCERT notes that areas with a comfortable climate, without much seasonal variation, attract more people, and that the Mediterranean regions were inhabited from early periods because of their pleasant climate.
Why not the others: Very hot or cold deserts (A, C) and areas of heavy rainfall such as the Amazon (D) are uncomfortable and are thinly populated.
Key point: Water, landforms, climate and soils are the geographical factors of population distribution.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport and Communication
questions.question: According to NCERT, which continent has one of the densest rail networks in the world?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Europe
Why: NCERT notes that Europe has one of the densest rail networks in the world, with about 4,40,000 km of railways, most of it double or multiple tracked.
Why not the others: Rail networks in Africa (A), South America (B) and Australia (C) are much less dense and mostly link interior areas with ports.
Key point: North America also has a dense network; railways there carry bulky goods over long distances.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Geography: Nature and Scope
questions.sub_topic: Definition of human geography by Semple
questions.question: Which geographer defined human geography as "the study of the changing relationship between the unresting man and the unstable earth"?
options: C) Paul Vidal de la Blache
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Ellen C. Semple
Why: NCERT quotes this definition from Ellen C. Semple; it stresses that both people and the earth keep changing.
Why not the others: Ratzel (A) called it the synthetic study of human societies and the earth's surface; Vidal de la Blache (C) spoke of a new conception of the relations between the earth and living beings; Griffith Taylor (D) is known for neo-determinism.
Key point: Semple was a student of Ratzel.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A country's population can fall between two censuses even though its birth rate is higher than its death rate.
Reason (R): Emigration always increases a country's population, because migrants send money home.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
Why: The Assertion is true — population change depends on births, deaths and migration together, so heavy emigration can outweigh a natural increase. The Reason is false — emigration reduces the population; remittances do not add people.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) need a true Reason; (D) needs a false Assertion.
Key point: Growth = (births − deaths) + (in-migrants − out-migrants).

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Human Settlements
questions.question: Which group consists only of towns that NCERT classifies as tourist towns?
options: A) Ambala, Jalandhar, Mhow and Babina
B) Nainital, Mussoorie, Pachmarhi and Mount Abu
C) Raniganj, Jharia, Digboi and Ankaleshwar
D) Roorkee, Aligarh, Pilani and Varanasi
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Nainital, Mussoorie, Pachmarhi and Mount Abu
Why: NCERT lists Nainital, Mussoorie, Shimla, Pachmarhi, Jodhpur, Jaisalmer, Udagamandalam (Ooty) and Mount Abu as tourist towns.
Why not the others: (A) are garrison towns; (C) are mining towns; (D) are educational towns.
Key point: Many hill stations were developed during the British period.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(A) Digboi
(B) Barauni
(C) Mumbai High
(D) Jharia

List-II
(I) Coalfield in the Damodar valley
(II) Offshore oilfield
(III) Market-based oil refinery
(IV) Field-based oil refinery
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: India has two types of refineries — field-based, such as Digboi (IV), and market-based, such as Barauni (III). Mumbai High is an offshore oilfield (II); Jharia is a coalfield of the Damodar valley (I).
Why not the others: (B) swaps the two refinery types; (C) swaps Barauni and Mumbai High; (D) swaps Mumbai High and Jharia.
Key point: Barauni is supplied by pipeline from the Assam oilfields.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Water Resources
questions.question: Which group consists of the four sources of surface water named by NCERT?
options: A) Rivers, lakes, ponds and tanks
B) Wells, tube wells, springs and canals
C) Glaciers, aquifers, wells and rain
D) Oceans, seas, bays and gulfs
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Rivers, lakes, ponds and tanks
Why: NCERT names rivers, lakes, ponds and tanks as the four major sources of surface water.
Why not the others: Wells and tube wells (B) and aquifers (C) draw groundwater; oceans and seas (D) are salt water.
Key point: The Ganga, Brahmaputra and Barak basins hold the largest share of surface water.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
questions.question: Dharavi, described by NCERT as one of the largest slums in Asia, is located in:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Mumbai
Why: NCERT's case study of a slum is Dharavi in Mumbai, with narrow lanes, crowded houses and poor civic amenities.
Why not the others: Kolkata (A), Delhi (C) and Chennai (D) also have large slums, but Dharavi is in Mumbai.
Key point: Slums are the home of many rural–urban migrants.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Development
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Growth is quantitative and value neutral.
(B) Development means a qualitative change, which is always value positive.
(C) Positive growth does not always lead to development.
(D) Any rise in a country's income automatically improves the quality of life of all its people.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: NCERT explains that growth is quantitative and may be positive or negative, while development is a qualitative, value-positive change; development occurs only when there is a positive change in quality, so growth alone is not enough.
Why not the others: (D) is false — higher income does not by itself improve everyone's quality of life. Options (A) and (B) include (D); option (D) leaves out the true statement (B).
Key point: Human development is about enlarging people's choices, not only incomes.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Water Resources
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Groundwater use is relatively low in states such as Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Kerala.
(B) Tamil Nadu has made water-harvesting structures compulsory in houses.
(C) Groundwater cannot be replenished once it has been used.
(D) Over-withdrawal of groundwater lowers the water table.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: (A) NCERT notes low groundwater use in Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Kerala. (B) In Tamil Nadu no building can be constructed without water-harvesting structures. (D) Over-use of groundwater has caused the water table to fall.
Why not the others: (C) is false — groundwater is a replenishable resource, recharged by rain and seepage; NCERT gives replenishable groundwater as about 432 cubic km. Options (A), (B) and (C) include (C).
Key point: Rainwater harvesting recharges aquifers and checks the falling water table.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport and Communication
questions.question: Pipelines are used extensively to carry which of the following over long distances without interruption?
options: A) Coal, iron ore, timber and steel goods
B) Cotton, jute, wool and food grains
D) Water, petroleum and natural gas
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Water, petroleum and natural gas
Why: NCERT notes that pipelines are used extensively to transport liquids and gases such as water, petroleum and natural gas; in some places they also carry slurry.
Why not the others: Bulky solids (A) and fibres and grain (B) usually move by rail, road or ship; passengers and mail (C) move by road, rail and air.
Key point: Pipelines give an uninterrupted flow and have low running costs once built.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Secondary Activities
questions.question: According to NCERT, which factor is the most important in the location of manufacturing industries?
options: A) The availability of cheap land for factories
B) Government subsidies offered to new units
C) The presence of a leader industry nearby
D) The existence of large markets for the goods
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) The existence of large markets for the goods
Why: NCERT states that the existence of large markets for manufactured goods is the most important factor in the location of industries — a market means people with demand and purchasing power.
Why not the others: Land (A), subsidies (B) and agglomeration with a leader industry (C) matter, but NCERT names markets first.
Key point: Developed regions of Europe, North America, Japan and Australia offer large global markets.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.sub_topic: Land-use categories by time left uncultivated
questions.question:
Arrange the following land-use categories in order of the length of time the land has been left uncultivated, from the shortest to the longest:
(A) Culturable waste-land
(B) Current fallow
(C) Net sown area
(D) Fallow other than current fallow
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (C), (B), (D), (A)
Why: Net sown area is cultivated in the current year (C); current fallow has been left uncultivated for one year or less (B); fallow other than current fallow for one to five years (D); culturable waste-land for more than five years (A).
Why not the others: (A) puts current fallow before net sown area; (B) puts the longer fallow before current fallow; (D) puts culturable waste-land before older fallow.
Key point: All these lands can be cultivated; barren and waste land cannot.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about changes in India's land use since 1950–51:
(A) The area under non-agricultural uses has increased at the highest rate.
(B) The area under forests has increased.
(C) Barren and waste land has declined.
(D) The area under permanent pastures and grazing land has increased.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: NCERT notes that land under non-agricultural uses has grown fastest, the area under forests has increased, and barren and waste land and culturable waste-land have declined.
Why not the others: (D) is false — the area under pastures and grazing land has declined, as it is taken over for cultivation and other uses. Every other option includes (D).
Key point: As an economy grows, land moves from agriculture to non-agricultural uses.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
questions.question: Smoke and fog often combine over Indian cities in winter. NCERT calls this:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Urban smog
Why: NCERT notes that air pollution causes smoky fog over cities, called urban smog; it is harmful to health.
Why not the others: Acid rain (A) is rain with dissolved sulphur and nitrogen oxides; ozone depletion (B) occurs in the upper atmosphere; a heat island (D) is a city warmer than its surroundings.
Key point: Air pollution affects the respiratory, nervous and circulatory systems.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Rice is the staple food of the overwhelming majority of people in India.
Reason (R): India is the second largest producer of rice in the world, after China.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both are true — NCERT describes rice as the staple food of most Indians and notes that India ranks second after China in rice production. But India's rank in world output does not explain why rice is eaten so widely; food habits and climate do.
Why not the others: (A) wrongly links the two; (C) and (D) need one statement to be false.
Key point: In West Bengal farmers grow three crops of rice a year — aus, aman and boro.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Water Resources
questions.question: Why is the level of groundwater use high in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh?
options: A) Industries there use most of the groundwater for cooling
B) Intensive irrigated farming of crops such as wheat and rice draws heavily on it
C) Rainfall there is so heavy that wells overflow every year
D) Their rivers are too polluted, so cities use only groundwater for drinking
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Intensive irrigated farming of crops such as wheat and rice draws heavily on it
Why: NCERT links the high use of groundwater in the north-western region with intensive irrigated agriculture; tube-well irrigation of water-demanding crops has caused the water table to fall.
Why not the others: Agriculture, not industry (A), is the main user; the region's rainfall is moderate to low (C); drinking water (D) is a small share of use.
Key point: In parts of these states, groundwater is being drawn faster than it is recharged.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: International Trade
questions.question: Which body is responsible for providing safe and efficient air traffic services in Indian air space and for managing India's airports?
options: A) The Airports Authority of India
C) The Indian Space Research Organisation
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) The Airports Authority of India
Why: NCERT notes that the Airports Authority of India provides air traffic and aeronautical communication services in Indian air space and manages the international and domestic airports.
Why not the others: Pawan Hans (B) runs helicopter services; ISRO (C) builds satellites; the Ministry of Shipping (D) deals with ports.
Key point: Air transport plays an important role in India's international trade of high-value goods.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Secondary Activities
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Industry)
(A) Sugar
(B) Copper smelting
(C) Plastics
(D) Paper

List-II (Class by raw material)
(I) Forest-based
(II) Chemical-based
(III) Mineral-based
(IV) Agro-based
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Sugar uses sugarcane (agro-based, IV); copper smelting uses ore (mineral-based, non-ferrous, III); plastics come from petrochemicals (chemical-based, II); paper uses wood, bamboo and grass (forest-based, I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps copper and plastics; (C) swaps sugar and copper; (D) swaps plastics and paper.
Key point: Mineral-based industries are ferrous (iron) or non-ferrous (copper, aluminium).

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.sub_topic: How land is cleared in shifting cultivation
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Two very different systems of farming are found in the tropics. Plantation agriculture was introduced by Europeans in their colonies. Its estates are large and need heavy capital investment, managerial and technical support and scientific methods of cultivation. Each estate specialises in a single crop, depends on cheap labour, and is linked by a good transport system to factories and ports, because most of the produce is processed and exported. Tea, coffee, cocoa, rubber, sugarcane, bananas and oil palm are typical plantation crops; some coffee fazendas of Brazil are still managed by Europeans.

Shifting cultivation is practised in the heavily forested areas of the Amazon basin, tropical Africa, parts of South-East Asia and North-East India. Farmers clear a patch of forest, grow crops with simple tools for a few years, and move to a new patch when the soil loses its fertility. As population grows and land becomes scarce, farmers return to the same patch sooner, and the cycle of jhum becomes shorter.

Question: In shifting cultivation, the vegetation on the forest patch is usually cleared by fire. What role do the ashes play?
options: A) They add to the fertility of the soil
B) They keep pests away for many years
C) They make the soil fit for heavy machines
D) They are sold to plantations as manure
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) They add to the fertility of the soil
Why: NCERT notes that the vegetation is usually cleared by fire and the ashes add to the fertility of the soil; this is why it is called slash-and-burn agriculture.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are not NCERT's description — farmers use simple tools, and the fertility from ash lasts only a few years.
Key point: Once fertility is lost, the farmer shifts to a new parcel of land.

Question: European powers set up plantations of different crops in their colonies. Which crop did the Dutch once hold a monopoly over in Indonesia?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Sugarcane
Why: NCERT notes that the Dutch once had a monopoly over sugarcane plantations in Indonesia.
Why not the others: Rubber (A) was planted by the British in Malaysia; oil palm (B) is not the crop NCERT links with the Dutch; coffee (C) was planted by the French in West Africa and on Brazil's fazendas.
Key point: The Spanish and Americans invested in coconut and sugarcane in the Philippines.

Question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of plantation agriculture, according to the passage and NCERT?
options: A) Large estates that need heavy capital investment
B) Specialisation in a single crop
C) A good transport link from the estate to factories and ports
D) Small plots cultivated mainly with family labour for home use
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Small plots cultivated mainly with family labour for home use
Why: Plantations are large, capital-intensive, single-crop estates using cheap hired labour, linked by transport to factories and markets for export.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are all features NCERT lists. (D) describes subsistence farming, not plantations.
Key point: Plantation agriculture is a commercial, export-oriented system.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.sub_topic: Effect of a shorter jhum cycle
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Two very different systems of farming are found in the tropics. Plantation agriculture was introduced by Europeans in their colonies. Its estates are large and need heavy capital investment, managerial and technical support and scientific methods of cultivation. Each estate specialises in a single crop, depends on cheap labour, and is linked by a good transport system to factories and ports, because most of the produce is processed and exported. Tea, coffee, cocoa, rubber, sugarcane, bananas and oil palm are typical plantation crops; some coffee fazendas of Brazil are still managed by Europeans.

Shifting cultivation is practised in the heavily forested areas of the Amazon basin, tropical Africa, parts of South-East Asia and North-East India. Farmers clear a patch of forest, grow crops with simple tools for a few years, and move to a new patch when the soil loses its fertility. As population grows and land becomes scarce, farmers return to the same patch sooner, and the cycle of jhum becomes shorter.

Question: The passage says the cycle of jhum is becoming shorter. What is the most likely result?
options: A) The forest grows back more thickly, so yields rise each cycle
B) The soil has too little time to recover, so yields fall
C) Farmers have to adopt plantation crops such as tea and rubber
D) Less forest needs to be burnt, so the soil becomes richer
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) The soil has too little time to recover, so yields fall
Why: In shifting cultivation the land is left fallow so that natural vegetation and fertility can return. When farmers come back sooner, the soil has not recovered, so fertility and yields decline.
Why not the others: A shorter fallow means less regrowth, not more (A, D); a shorter cycle does not by itself turn farms into plantations (C).
Key point: NCERT notes that the shrinking jhum cycle leads to a loss of fertility.

Question: Which of the following correctly pairs a European power, a plantation crop it established and the region where it did so?
options: A) French — cocoa and coffee — West Africa
B) British — sugarcane and bananas — Indonesia
C) Dutch — tea and coffee — Sri Lanka
D) Spanish — rubber and oil palm — Malaysia
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) French — cocoa and coffee — West Africa
Why: NCERT notes that the French established cocoa and coffee plantations in West Africa.
Why not the others: Indonesia's sugarcane was a Dutch monopoly (B); tea in Sri Lanka was British (C); rubber in Malaysia was British (D).
Key point: The British also set up sugarcane and banana plantations in the West Indies.
